meta.description:
Manages, constructs, repairs, and modifies structural systems and wooden, masonry, metal, and concrete buildings. Fabricates and repairs components of buildings, utility systems, and real property equipment. Ensures compliance with environmental regulations. 
Duties and Responsibilities: 
- Prepares and interprets working drawings and schematics for maintaining, altering, and repairing buildings and structures. Surveys proposed work sites to determine material and labor requirements. Prepares cost estimates. Reviews structural work progress and coordinates changes in schedules. Constructs and repairs footings, floors, slabs, foundations, walls, roofs, steps, doors, and windows for prefabricated and permanent structures. Constructs and modifies buildings. Prepares, applies, and finishes mortar, concrete, plaster, and stucco. Fabricates repairs and installs metal parts and assemblies for utility systems and buildings. 
- Erects steel and lays out trusses and structures to specific dimensions. Welds, cuts, brazes, and solders ferrous and nonferrous metals using various welding processes. Welds butt, lap, tee, and edge joints in all working positions. Inspects, maintains, repairs, and installs overhead and rollup doors, and mechanical gates. Installs forms and reinforcing material. Applies protective coatings such as primers, stains, and sealants. 
- Troubleshoots, repairs, and installs commercially manufactured locking devices such as keyed, combination, cipher, panic hardware/exit device, and pad locks. 
- Erects scaffolding and works from ladders and mobile platforms. 
- Identifies and selects construction materials considering strength, moisture content, grade, mix, application procedures, and curing. 
- Manages, inspects, and evaluates work center activities. Ensures compliance with commercial and military publications. Submits and reviews supply and equipment requisitions. Discusses inspection findings and recommends corrective action.

meta.medicalFacility:
Anytime a military member is injured ON or OFF duty or an Air Force civilian is injured ON duty, or there is damage to government property or equipment, the mishap must be investigated and reported to 436/512 AW/SE regardless of severity. A good rule to follow is if a person gets injured and seeks medical treatment, it's serious enough to be investigated and reported to a supervisor and Wing Safety Office.
It is important to note that if a mishap is very serious (fatality, amputation, serious bodily injury, in-patient hospitalization of personnel, suspected property damage of over $2,000 etc...) notification of Wing SEG is required.
Supervisors shall know, and be briefed on the requirement to complete AF Form 978, Mishap Report of Injury/Illness and Treatment for mishaps that happen to their workers. If your subordinate is treated and cannot fill out the form then the supervisor is required to complete and sign the mishap form. This form must be completely filled out and signed. Turn this form into the Unit Safety Representative for forwarding to Wing Safety.
The AF Form 978, Supervisor’s Mishap Report helps you to record the facts as soon as possible after the incident before a significant amount of time has passed. The AF Form 978 must be used to document all mishap (personnel) injuries. You can obtain blank forms from EPUBS, your Unit Safety Representative or from the Wing Safety EIM page.
Mandatory: individuals and supervisors must provide documents if seen at an off-base facility to report incident/illness. Many times the Primary Care Manager cannot see the patient until a few days have passed. Any information that can be gathered regarding the incident helps all safety personnel involved plan ahead.
For both military and civilian members, light duty assignments may be available. The Air Force wants to make every effort to return injured employees to duty as soon as the attending physician deems feasible. To reduce lost time and to help employees maintain their pay status, options are available to provide light duty work for those who are capable. This could include answer telephones, filing, mail distribution or other duties that may be within the capacity of the injured party.

meta.activeShooterMethods:
Assess Situation:
Determine most reasonable way to protect your own life
Do Not confuse Lockdown with Shelter-In-Place response
React:
Determine the location of the shooter (inside or outside). Key decision factors:
(1) Your proximity to the shooter
(2) The accessibility of egress routes.
Shooter may be moving through the facility or the parking areas. Be aware of the incident in regard to crossfire between the attacker and responding Security Forces.
Call Security Forces:
When safe: contact Security Forces: use local procedures!
(1) ESCAPE (Run or Evacuate):
If the shooter is in the facility and it is safe to do so, evacuate (escape) from the facility.
Once outside, all personnel should disperse and take cover until the threat has been neutralized.
(2) BARRICADE (Lockdown):
Barricade yourself in a lock room; close/lock all windows, close blinds and turn off all lights, silence cell phones.
If door cannot be locked; block with desks, chairs, etc.
(3) FIGHT (Take Action):
As a last resort and only when your life is in imminent danger – attempt to incapacitate the shooter. Act with physical aggression and throw items
